items.prompt: We’ve seen that fractions can represent division. Now, we can use that fact to convert a number from fraction form into decimal form. For example, this fraction can be read as fifty-two over one hundred.  52/100  It can also be read as fifty-two divided by one hundred, which is this, in decimal form.
items.demo: Fifty-two divided by one hundred, in decimal form, is *0.52*.

items.prompt: Watch what I change.  47/100  Forty-seven hundredths, or forty-seven divided by one hundred.
items.demo: Forty-seven hundredths in decimal form is *0.47*.

items.prompt: Once more, watch what I change.  7/100  Seven hundredths, or seven divided by one hundred.
items.demo: Seven hundredths in decimal form is *0.07*.

items.prompt: Your turn. Rewrite in decimal form.  31/100
Ben writes 7/100 as 0.7. Is Ben right? How do you know?
items.expected: No. 0.7 is seven tenths. Seven hundredths needs a zero in the tenths column, so it is 0.07.
items.demo: *No*. 0.7 is seven tenths. Seven hundredths needs a zero in the tenths column, so it is 0.07.
